warnings: LOW-INFORMATIONAL (non-blocking; Coder-facing, already adequately specified). Because the override is placed at :8239 (upstream of the split_k computation at :8252), guard #8's split_k==1 requirement must be evaluated against the AXIOM pipeline's wg_denoms (the value :8252 will actually use), not the stock pipeline's. I verified this is fail-closed under BOTH readings, so it does NOT block: (i) at the target shape M=4096,N=512,K=14336, AXIOM's {32,32,1} gives m_tiles*n_tiles = 128*16 = 2048; ggml_vk_guess_split_k (:7754) only raises split_k>1 when m_tiles*n_tiles <= shader_core_count/2, i.e. core_count >= 4096 SMs — no GPU exists, so split_k is unconditionally 1 there; (ii) more generally, AXIOM's 32x32 tile yields MORE tiles (larger product) than any stock large/medium tile, and split_k is monotonically non-increasing in the tile-product, so stock_split_k >= axiom_split_k — hence a guard that checks stock split_k==1 is a SUFFICIENT (conservative) proxy for axiom_split_k==1, and a guard that checks the AXIOM pipeline is exact. Either way there is no path on which the AXIOM kernel (which does not implement k_split partial-K accumulation) is dispatched with split_k>1. Guard #8 already lists split_k==1 with the correct :8252 citation, so the requirement is captured; I flag only that the Coder should compute #8 from the AXIOM pipeline / after :8252 (or rely on the conservative stock proxy) to keep the invariant self-evident.
